transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62m
Attendees: Jordan Price (Redwood AE), Maya Li (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (CTO - Celestia), Brian Turner (DevOps), Sana Patel (Security)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on private networking options (VPC Peering vs PrivateLink), data residency/regions, egress limits, and benchmark plan (workload sizing, success criteria, timelines). Agreed to send architecture doc and benchmark runbook; customer to confirm regions and constraints.

Topics:
- Private connectivity: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway
- Regions & data residency (us-east-1, eu-west-1 mostly)
- Egress and corporate proxy constraints
- Success criteria for POC: latency/99p, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, functional correctness
- Benchmark plan: sample payloads, sequence lengths, concurrency, KV cache priming

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about an hour. Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this one. Maya from our infra team is with me. Alicia, Brian, Sana, can you hear us?
00:10 Alicia: Yes, hear you. Thanks, Jordan. Appreciate the time.
00:15 Jordan: Awesome. Quick agenda — nail down networking approach for the POC, confirm regions, talk success criteria and the benchmark plan. Maya, do you want to kick off on connectivity options?
00:27 Maya: Sure. So high level — we support three main private networking patterns for POCs: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (our sidecar NLB + ENI approach), and Transit Gateway for multi-VPC. For most customers wanting private connectivity without egress over public internet, PrivateLink is simplest because it keeps traffic inside the AWS backbone and we don't require route table changes on the customer side. Peering works too but has cross-account route complexity and scale limits.
00:55 Brian: Quick question — our infra team prefers VPC peering because we can monitor routes more easily; we also use a corporate proxy for egress. Will that break anything?
01:05 Maya: The corporate proxy can be an issue if it's intercepting outbound TLS. With PrivateLink, traffic goes to an interface endpoint in your VPC and you don't traverse NAT/proxy the same way. With peering, traffic is routed over the peered CIDR ranges — if your proxy inspects or forces egress, you may still hit policy. We usually recommend PrivateLink when customers have strict egress/proxy policies.
01:30 Sana: To add, from a security perspective, we need to ensure no customer data is routed over public egress and that audit logs are available. Does Redwood provide flow logs or access logs for the PrivateLink endpoints?
01:42 Maya: We can enable VPC flow logs on the components we control in the Dedicated/private deployment. For hosted PrivateLink we'll provide connection logs and request traces surfaced in the Console. There may be some PII in logs so we can redact or configure retention per your compliance needs.
02:00 Jordan: For the POC, is Celestia leaning toward Dedicated capacity in a private VPC or a Private deployment?
02:08 Alicia: We're evaluating both — Dedicated is attractive for performance predictability, but Private (VPC-controlled) is required for some datasets due to residency and audit requirements. For the proof we want to validate the Private networking setup and perf with our sample workloads.
02:25 Jordan: Got it. Let's scope the workload then. Brian, what are the typical request sizes and concurrency you expect?
02:32 Brian: Our typical inference calls are text generation for summaries — usually 512 to 2k tokens, average 800 tokens; peak concurrent requests around 40-60 during batch jobs, and sustained 8-10 qps for interactive tools. We also plan a nightly batch of 50k docs for embeddings but that's later.
02:58 Maya: That helps. For the benchmark we'll want to test two payload profiles: interactive (800 tokens median, 10 qps sustained, bursts to 60 concurrent) and batch generation (2k tokens, throughput oriented). We'll also test KV cache priming for session affinity to measure RT improvements.
03:20 Alicia: Success criteria — for the interactive flow we want 99th percentile latency under 350ms per token and overall end-to-end under 1.2s for shorter prompts, and cost target of <= $0.30 per 1k tokens for the POC baseline. Is that reasonable?
03:38 Jordan: Those are reasonable targets for a Dedicated-backed profile with quantized weights and batching tuned. We'll need to validate on your chosen model size. Which model did you want to run?
03:48 Alicia: We'd like to try an open LLM equivalent to ~13B param that you've validated (we're not moving to Anthropic or Bedrock right now).
03:56 Maya: We have a few verified 13B variants — we'll pick one with a quantization profile that balances accuracy and latency. For cost, caching (prefix and KV) and batching will have a big impact. Our Optimize recommendations will include batch sizes for your workload.
04:15 Brian: On regions — we need the service to run in us-east-1 for primary and eu-west-1 for EU customers. Can PrivateLink be set up in both regions?
04:25 Maya: Yes. We can provision endpoints in both regions. For Private (customer VPC) deployments we can deploy behind your VPC in the target region. There is some lead time for DNS and cert provisioning across regions — usually 3-5 business days per region for a POC.
04:41 Sana: Data residency: any logs or persisted metadata from inference stored outside region? We need assurances that model artifacts or cache snapshots aren't replicated to another region without consent.
04:52 Jordan: Good callout. For Private deployments we honor region scoping; we can ensure no cross-region replication of KV cache or persisted artifacts. For hosted Dedicated there are options to pin instances to a region and prevent backups outside region. We'll provide contract language for data residency.
05:08 Maya: Also note that if you use our managed model catalog and pull-model updates, model binaries may be staged in our infra for onboarding — we can disable auto-updates during the POC to keep artifacts stable and region-local.
05:22 Brian: Egress constraints — we have a hard egress cap of 5 TB/month per environment for POC due to cost approvals and our proxy enforces it. How do we measure egress and keep within limits?
05:33 Maya: We expose token counts and network egress in the Console. For the benchmark we will provide an estimate of network egress based on sequence lengths and number of calls. Also we can run the tests in your VPC so bulk data transfer to S3 or external endpoints will be under your control.
05:48 Jordan: For the benchmark plan, we'll create a matrix: payload profile, qps, concurrency, model variant, enabled caching, and expected metrics (99p latency, median latency, tokens/sec, egress MB). That will let us run a deterministic run and compare.
06:02 Alicia: Perfect. Timeline then? We want to kick the POC next week if possible. What are realistic lead times?
06:09 Maya: If you already have an account and entitlements, PrivateLink provisioning + basic Dedicated infra takes about 3-5 business days. Benchmarks we can run in 2-3 days once infra is up and sample data is provided. So earliest end-to-end initial results in about 10 business days.
06:25 Jordan: So target: infra provisioned by 2026-04-22, benchmark plan and scripts by 2026-04-22, runs completed by 2026-04-28, follow-up review 2026-04-29. Does that align?
06:36 Alicia: Sounds tight but ok. We'll confirm internal approvals.
06:41 Brian: About security review — our InfoSec will need SOC2 Type II attestation, SAML/SSO integration, and KMS integration. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
06:53 Jordan: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS or HSM, and SAML/SCIM for SSO. We can share the security pack.
07:03 Sana: For audit logs we need a 12-month retention and export to our log sink. Can that be configured?
07:10 Maya: We can set retention policies and push logs to your S3 or CloudWatch log group for the POC — long-term retention and export will be part of the Private deployment agreement.
07:20 Alicia: A few clarification points on success criteria: 1) Accuracy/regression — we will run a small eval set of 500 prompts and want no more than 5% drop vs baseline, 2) Latency targets as discussed, 3) Cost estimate baseline. We'll include those in the doc.
07:38 Jordan: Great. We'll include an Eval partition in the benchmark runbook. Maya, anything on the bench infra?
07:45 Maya: We'll prefer to run the load generators in your VPC (containerized) to avoid extra egress and get realistic networking topology. We'll need an endpoint to push results and a bastion for logs. Also we'll instrument KV cache warm-up to measure warm vs cold latencies.
08:05 Brian: For the load generator, we can spin up an EC2 autoscaled fleet or a k8s job — we'll coordinate.
08:12 Jordan: Any other blockers?
08:15 Alicia: One more — pricing for Dedicated for the POC: do you have a short-term trial rate?
08:21 Jordan: We typically do a time-limited POC pricing with reduced reserved commit or trial credits. I'll include pricing scenarios in the follow-up email (dedicated hourly vs reserved).
08:30 Maya: Also, note model quantization choices will affect both latency and output quality. We'll recommend a 4-bit quantized profile for latency, and keep a float16 variant for accuracy checks.
08:42 Sana: If we see regressions in quality with quantization, can we fall back to float16 during canary?
08:48 Maya: Yes — we support rollout policies and automatic fallback to a different model variant if you configure it. That's built into our Console rollouts.
08:58 Jordan: Alright let's recap next steps and owners.
09:01 Jordan: Jordan will send the PrivateLink/VPC peering architecture doc, compliance pack, and preliminary pricing by 2026-04-20.
09:08 Maya: I'll draft the benchmark runbook and the exact test matrix and sample script; target 2026-04-22.
09:14 Alicia: We'll confirm regions and POC success criteria doc by 2026-04-21, and provide sample prompt set and a small dataset for eval.
09:23 Brian: I'll provide egress limits and decide if we want VPC peering or PrivateLink for the initial run — due 2026-04-21.
09:30 Sana: Our InfoSec will review the security pack; I'll coordinate and get back with questions by 2026-04-23.
09:38 Jordan: Great. Anything else?
09:40 Alicia: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
09:44 Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling links.
09:48 (call ends)
